summary: Independent review of 54 runs (27 E. coli cultures x Lys-C/P fraction 1 + Trypsin/P fraction 2) found no blocking or important issues. Sample-to-file, fraction and enzyme mapping reproduce the deposited MaxQuant summary.txt with 0 mismatches; every deposited RAW file is claimed exactly once; official validator, check, score and structure pass. Only minor findings remain.

design_consistency.evidence: 27 source names = 27 MaxQuant experiments (BL21(DE3) 4, H10407 3, H608 3, TW10598 4, TW10722 3, TW10828 3, TW11681 3, TW14425 4); each source has exactly two runs, fraction 1 = Lys-C/P (_L) and fraction 2 = Trypsin/P (_T), matching summary.txt Fraction column and the protocol statement that LysC and tryptic fractions of the same replicate were combined. Biological replicate indices match MaxQuant experiment suffixes; technical replicate 1 throughout; factor value[strain or breed] equals characteristics[strain or breed]; both runs of each source share one lc batch (0 sources with >1 batch). Label free sample on all rows.

omission_safety.evidence: Every nontrivial value traced to PRIDE record, MaxQuant summary.txt, abstract or raw-file content. No reagent, age/sex, lineage, serotype or colonization-factor values added; organism part/cell type/disease set to 'not applicable' for pure bacterial cultures (allowed by TERMS.tsv). ms2 analyzer given as generic 'ion trap' (less specific than evidence, safe). H608 strain label is the depositor's own file label (alias HA608 in MaxQuant), disclosed as a limitation; no unsupported specificity found.

findings.message: tools reconcile flags 'Lys-C/P' and 'Trypsin/P' as contradicting/incomplete versus the record's 'trypsin and LysC'. Adjudicated as a lexical false positive: the dataProcessingProtocol states 'allowing N-terminal cleavage to proline' and summary.txt lists Enzyme LysC/P on every _L run and Trypsin/P on every _T run, so the /P terms are the deposited per-run specificities.
findings.evidence: PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol; MaxQuant output txt/summary.txt Enzyme column.

findings.message: 20 ppm is the MaxQuant initial (first-search) precursor tolerance stated in the protocol; the main-search tolerance under MaxQuant standard settings would be 4.5 ppm, which is not stated in the deposit. Value is literally supported; optionally note the first-search context.
findings.evidence: dataProcessingProtocol: 'The initial allowed mass deviation of the precursor ion was as high as 20 ppm'; 'Standard settings were used'.

findings.location: characteristics[strain or breed] / factor value[strain or breed] rows 15-20
findings.message: 'H608' is the depositor's file label; MaxQuant names the same runs HA608 (experiments HA-1..HA-3) and no public strain record was found in Europe PMC for H608/HA608. Acceptable as the depositor label and disclosed in the manifest; resolve to the published designation if the full paper becomes available.
findings.evidence: PRIDE file names H608_*.raw; summary.txt HA608_*; Europe PMC searches '"HA608"' and '"H608" AND coli' returned no relevant hits.

findings.message: Values are the acquisition-session folder names embedded in each raw header (8 sessions, e.g. 2015-01-23_OrbitrapElite_Unknown); they act as an acquisition/LC session proxy rather than a documented LC batch. Sessions partly confound with replicate index across strains (e.g. 2014-01-24 holds replicate 1 of H608, TW10598, TW10828), which is a property of the experiment, not an annotation error.
findings.evidence: Raw header paths in all 54 files contain the stated folder string; both runs of every source share one session.
